outcomes.name: Bone health (fractures)
outcomes.population: general midlife/older adults not selected for deficiency or osteoporosis
outcomes.sentence: 2000 IU D3 daily did not reduce fractures in 25,871 adults over 5.3 years (HR 0.98, CI 0.89–1.08).

ledger.effect_basis: VITAL null plus MAs of D monotherapy RR 1.00 (0.95-1.06) high-certainty in community adults
ledger.effective_daily_range: none for D alone in this population; 400-800 IU plus calcium in high-risk/deficient/institutionalized

effect.found: No reduction in total, non-vertebral or hip fractures.
effect.missing: A modest hip-fracture drop appears only with added calcium in older high-risk groups.

evidence.found: Pivotal large RCT at this exact dose plus consistent meta-analyses of D alone.

form.found: Daily oral D3 matches VITAL and most included trials.

dose.found: 2000 IU is the precise VITAL dose tested.

outcomes.name: Immune (respiratory infections)
outcomes.population: general adults (historical signal limited to deficient people on daily 400–1000 IU)
outcomes.sentence: Latest meta-analysis of 61,000 people: no overall reduction in respiratory infections (OR 0.94, CI 0.88–1.00). VITAL 2000 IU also null.

ledger.effect_basis: 2025 MA CI includes 1; 1001-2000 IU subgroup 0.97 (0.92-1.01); VITAL daily 2000 IU OR 0.96
ledger.effective_daily_range: 400-1000 IU daily possibly in deficient; 2000 IU not shown effective

effect.found: No overall reduction in respiratory infections at this dose.
effect.missing: An older pooled analysis suggested 12–19% fewer infections in daily-dose or deficient subgroups.
effect.move: None for general adults at this dose.

evidence.found: Updated large-trial meta-analysis is null; VITAL daily 2000 IU null.

form.found: Daily oral D3 was historically the better regimen.

dose.found: 2000 IU sits in the 1001–2000 IU bin, which showed no effect.

outcomes.name: Mood (depressive symptoms)
outcomes.population: general adults 50+ without current clinically relevant depression
outcomes.sentence: 2000 IU D3 for 5.3 years did not change depression incidence or mood scores in 18,353 adults (HR 0.97).
